exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: Children born in Taiwan in 2005, from the Taiwan Birth Cohort Study
finding: While children born by cesarean section had higher rates of neurodevelopmental disorders, asthma, and obesity, only the association with obesity remained significant after controlling for gestational age at birth and other relevant factors.
mod_finding: The association between cesarean section and childhood neurodevelopmental disorders was attenuated after controlling for gestational age at birth, and there was no significant association between cesarean section and childhood asthma after controlling for parental history of asthma and gestational age at birth.
